2020/HSCTF/crypto/Affina_and_the_Quadrat: Quadratic homework moonlights as an affine cipher in HSCTF 2020's Affina and the Quadratics. Its coefficients give the game away.
2020/HSCTF/crypto/Chonky_E/2020-06-06-HS: HSCTF 2020's Chonky E skimps on the private exponent: Boneh-Durfee cracks RSA, and shared primes take Schmidt-Samoa down with it.
2020/HSCTF/crypto/Extremely_Complex_Chal: SageMath has a modest workload in HSCTF 2020's Extremely Complex Challenge: recover an elliptic-curve parameter, then solve a decidedly small discrete log.
2020/HSCTF/crypto/Morbid/2020-06-06-HSCT: Nine symbols, 9! keys, one brute-force budget: decode Morbit's Morse pairs in HSCTF 2020's Morbid.
2020/HSCTF/crypto/Randomization_1/2020-0: HSCTF 2020's Randomization 1 brings 8 bits of LCG state to a guessing game. Ghidra helps put all ten predictions on the answer sheet.
2020/HSCTF/crypto/Randomization_2/2020-0: The exposed 64-bit LCG state in HSCTF 2020's Randomization 2 does the fortune-telling for us. Python just needs to remember to overflow.
2020/HSCTF/crypto/Smol_E/2020-06-06-HSCT: HSCTF 2020's Smol E pads RSA messages on a budget. Coppersmith finds the short-pad difference; Franklin-Reiter finishes the decryption.
2020/HSCTF/crypto/Unexpected/2020-06-06-: Three RSA moduli borrow each other's primes in HSCTF 2020's Unexpected. Pairwise GCDs collect the debt and let us decrypt.
2020/HSCTF/crypto/XORed/2020-06-06-HSCTF: XOR's cancellation policy does the work in HSCTF 2020's XORed: recover the message without recovering each individual key first.
2020/HSCTF/crypto/xkcd_com_2247_v2/2020-: Invert a 100-by-100 Hill cipher key modulo 26 in HSCTF 2020's XKCD 2247 v2. Bring SageMath, leave the graph paper.
2020/HSCTF/miscellaneous/N-95/2020-06-06: QR code surgery in HSCTF 2020's N-95: rebuild the grid, recover the mask pattern and brute-force missing bits. The scanner needs backup.
2020/batpwn/crypto/Cryptographer/2020-06: BATPWN 2020's Cryptographer spells its timestamp XOR key in ASCII zeroes and ones. Each key byte has just two career options.
2020/batpwn/crypto/M-ick_Maybe/2020-06-0: Proofreading is cryptanalysis in BATPWN 2020's M-ick Maybe: solve a substitution cipher, then diff it against Moby Dick for stowaway characters.
2020/batpwn/crypto/prefixes/2020-06-08-B: Go's shifts and XORs get a reverse gear in BATPWN 2020's Prefixes: test all 256 byte values and reconstruct the input one character at a time.
2020/nahamconCTF/crypto/December/2020-06: Four weak DES keys audition for NahamCon 2020's December. OFB decryption gives one the part.
2020/nahamconCTF/crypto/Docxor/2020-06-1: ZIP magic bytes earn their wizard hat in NahamCon 2020's Docxor: recover a four-byte XOR key from the header and restore the document.
2020/nahamconCTF/crypto/Homecooked/2020-: NahamCon 2020's Homecooked leaves its prime-palindrome XOR decoder simmering in trial division. gmpy2's primality test cuts the cooking time.
2020/nahamconCTF/crypto/Ooo-la-la/2020-0: RSA's primes are a little too neighborly in NahamCon 2020's Ooo-la-la. Alpertron factors the modulus so decryption can proceed.
2020/nahamconCTF/crypto/Raspberry/2020-0: NahamCon 2020's Raspberry packs RSA with snack-sized primes. Factor them, compute the totient and unwrap the ciphertext.
2020/nahamconCTF/crypto/Twinning/2020-06: A gap of two is poor personal space for RSA primes: a square root factors the modulus in NahamCon 2020's Twinning and unlocks the PIN.
2020/nahamconCTF/crypto/Unvreakable_Vase: Base64 lost its uppercase letters in NahamCon 2020's Unvreakable Vase. A four-character brute-force loop joins the case-sensitive repair crew.
2020/nahamconCTF/crypto/elsa4/2020-06-14: A timestamp is the LC4 seed suspect in NahamCon 2020's elsa4. The investigation is still frozen at nonce handling, which remains unresolved.
2020/ractf/crypto/01/2020-06-09-RACTF-20: RACTF 2020's 01 swaps the alphabet and misplaces the spaces. quipqiup solves the monoalphabetic substitution; word spacing still needs a human.
2020/ractf/crypto/02/2020-06-09-RACTF-20: The alphabet keeps changing shifts in RACTF 2020's 02. Identify Vigenere and let dCode fish out the key.
2020/ractf/crypto/03/2020-06-09-RACTF-20: Letter frequencies rat out a transposition in RACTF 2020's 03. The plaintext took a five-rail fence detour.
2020/ractf/crypto/04/2020-06-09-RACTF-20: RACTF 2020's 04 shuffles columns but leaves English letter frequencies on the nametag. A visual solver undoes the columnar transposition.
2020/ractf/crypto/05/2020-06-09-RACTF-20: RACTF 2020's 05 forgot to disguise its statistics. They point to Bifid; CryptoCrack handles the decryption.
2020/ractf/crypto/06/2020-06-09-RACTF-20: Periodic Gromark needs a numeric primer; RACTF 2020's 06 packed one for us. CryptoCrack takes it from there.
2020/ractf/crypto/B007L36_CRYP70_4641N/2: RACTF 2020's B007L36 CRYP70 A641N puts on Base64 camouflage. Underneath, repeating-key addition lets known plaintext recover the key by subtraction.
2020/ractf/crypto/BOO7l3G_CRYP70/2020-06: The random four-number blocks in RACTF 2020's BOO7l3G CRYP70 keep changing outfits but not their sums. Addition recovers the encoded characters.
2020/ractf/crypto/Its_as_easy_as_access0: Promote yourself by XOR in RACTF 2020's It's as easy as access=0000: flip AES-CBC IV bits to edit a guest token into admin credentials.
2020/ractf/crypto/Mysterious_Masqueradin: RACTF 2020's Mysterious Masquerading Message wears an SSH private-key costume. Decode its clues to find the key and IV for AES-CBC decryption.
2020/ractf/crypto/Really_Secret_Algorith: The walrus operator isn't a vault. RACTF 2020's Really Secret Algorithm hides RSA primes behind reversible running XOR and Base85.
2020/ractf/crypto/Really_Simple_Algorith: RACTF 2020's Really Simple Algorithm ships RSA with p and q included. Compute the private exponent and decrypt; the factoring department has the day off.
2020/ractf/crypto/Really_Small_Algorithm: A tiny RSA prime gives trial division a job in RACTF 2020's Really Small Algorithm. Find the factor, then decrypt with modular arithmetic.
2020/ractf/crypto/Really_Speedy_Algorith: RACTF 2020's Really Speedy Algorithm puts RSA on a shot clock: parse the prompts and script the missing parameters for 100 timed questions.
2020/redpwn/crypto/12-shades-of-redpwn/2: redpwnCTF 2020's 12 Shades of Redpwn makes the color wheel do arithmetic. Map hues to base-12 digits and convert the result to text.
2020/redpwn/crypto/4k-rsa/2020-06-27-red: A large RSA modulus made of smaller primes is factorization's bulk discount in redpwnCTF 2020's 4k-rsa. Recover the factors and decryption exponent.
2020/redpwn/crypto/alien-transmissions-v: Even aliens have word-spacing habits. Frequency analysis recovers a combined XOR key in redpwnCTF 2020's Alien Transmissions v2; Z3 splits it in two.
2020/redpwn/crypto/base646464/2020-06-27: redpwnCTF 2020's base646464 applies Base64 25 times. A Python decode loop respectfully declines to call that encryption.
2020/redpwn/crypto/itsy-bitsy/2020-06-27: Leading bits in this random XOR keystream insist on being 1. Their predictable habits expose the plaintext in redpwnCTF 2020's Itsy Bitsy.
2020/redpwn/crypto/primimity/2020-06-27-: Three RSA primes share a postcode in redpwnCTF 2020's primimity. Search near the modulus's cube root to find the factors.
2020/redpwn/crypto/pseudo-key/2020-06-27: A Vigenere key encrypts itself in redpwnCTF 2020's Pseudo-key, leaving 2,048 candidates. Self-care would have involved a different key.
2020/redpwn/crypto/worst-pw-manager/2020: Eight Python references in a trench coat pose as an RC4 key in redpwnCTF 2020's worst-pw-manager. Decode filenames, then brute-force the repeated key byte.
2020/rgbctf/crypto/Adequate_Encryption_S: rgbCTF 2020's Adequate Encryption Standard has a custom cipher whose key schedule gets stuck on 0 or 1. Reverse the rounds and exploit the rut.
2020/rgbctf/crypto/N-AES/2020-07-13-rgbC: rgbCTF 2020's N-AES has more layers than entropy: brute-force a fixed one-byte seed to undo 128 AES layers, minding Python's int-versus-bytes seed trap.
2020/tctf/crypto/babyring/2020-06-30-TCT: 0CTF/TCTF 2020's babyring makes RC4 run in circles. Reduce the ring check to XOR equations and let SageMath choose RSA inputs that close the loop.
2020/zh3r0/crypto/Analyze_me/2020-06-18-: zh3r0 CTF 2020's Analyze Me can't pick a base. Decode the mixed-base chunks, then undo XOR and repeated byte substitutions in the second act.
2020/zh3r0/crypto/Double_fish/2020-06-18: zh3r0 CTF 2020's Double Fish pairs Deadfish with Blowfish-CBC and an XOR-masked key. A stray escape sequence makes this fishing trip harder.
2020/zh3r0/crypto/Hastads_message/2020-0: RSA repeats itself but forgets to introduce e in zh3r0 CTF 2020's Hastad's Message. Try exponents with CRT and integer roots for the broadcast attack.
2020/zh3r0/crypto/Mix/2020-06-18-zh3r0-2: zh3r0 CTF 2020's Mix serves Base65536 with keyboard-shift clues and a Spoon esolang finish. Decoding comes with cutlery.
2020/zh3r0/crypto/RSA-Warmup/2020-06-18-: SymPy finds the small prime that skipped leg day in zh3r0 CTF 2020's RSA Warmup. Factor the modulus, then decrypt with the recovered key.
2020/zh3r0/crypto/Uncipher_me/2020-06-18: zh3r0 CTF 2020's Uncipher Me sends us on an encoded-key scavenger hunt. The ROT47-derived key opens the Fernet token; the other keys are busywork.
2020/zh3r0/crypto/We_are_related/2020-06: Chosen suffixes give RSA messages a family resemblance in zh3r0 CTF 2020's We Are Related. Franklin-Reiter recovers the shared plaintext.
2020/zh3r0/crypto/gboad_maddy/2020-06-19: Gboard's alternate symbols get promoted to ciphertext in zh3r0 CTF 2020's gboad maddy. Map them to letters, apply ROT13 and infer the missing characters.
2021/google_ctf/crypto/pythia/2021-07-21: Google CTF 2021's Pythia has commitment issues: AES-GCM key multicollisions turn a partitioning oracle into a short-password recovery tool.
2022/cyber_apocalypse/crypto/memory_acce: HTB Cyber Apocalypse 2022's Memory Acceleration puts Z3 on a diet: brute-force part of a custom proof-of-work hash and model the smaller remainder.
2022/google_ctf/crypto/maybe_someday/202: Google CTF 2022's Maybe Someday plays twenty questions in one batch. Paillier's homomorphic addition makes the padding oracle distinguish secrets.
2022/sdctf/crypto/tasty_crypto_roll/2022: SDCTF 2022's Tasty Crypto Roll seasons its key with a PID. Recover it, undo bit shuffling and let Z3 solve the ECB substitution constraints.
2023/ACSC/crypto/SusCipher/2023-03-01-AC: ACSC 2023's SusCipher gets cross-examined by Z3: 48 single-bit plaintexts give a model enough evidence to recover the three-round block cipher's key.
2023/nullcon_hackim/crypto/curvy_decrypt: Nullcon HackIM 2023's Curvy Decryptor admits off-curve guests. Shift EC points past the decryption filter, then recover the private key with invalid curves and CRT.
